Parse-model agreement between libxml2 (this SDK) and the JS family.
purpose: A tokenized phrase's key IS its encoded string, so any disagreement about how the DOM is BUILT changes the key before canonicalisation is even reached. Canonicalisation cannot close these; only the parser can.
js_family_source: langsys-js-server @ 8105faa, real Chromium 153 measured against parse5 over these same families: 9 of 9 agreed, so these are the JS-FAMILY answer rather than one engine's.
measured_by: langsys-php-sdk on PHP 8.3.19 with libxml2 2.9.13 (LIBXML_DOTTED_VERSION), via DOMDocument::loadHTML with LIBXML_HTML_NOIMPLIED|LIBXML_HTML_NODEFDTD. The test wraps each fragment in a <div> to give the tokenizer a root; the real translatePage route (PageTranslator::parseDocument) reproduces every value identically, verified both ways. Every libxml2 column in this file is scoped to that version.
agreement: 3 of 7 ON LIBXML2 2.9.13 - implied close agrees 3/3; raw text 0/2 and foster parenting 0/2 diverge. VERSION-BOUND, not a property of libxml2: the Reviewer measured lxml on libxml2 2.14.6 giving the JS-family tokens on all seven inputs, and Nokogiri on libxml2 2.13.9 behaving like 2.9.13. The boundary lies between 2.13.9 and 2.14.6; no cause is stated because none was measured. PHP takes libxml2 from the PHP build, which composer cannot pin, so these ids move when a host's libxml2 crosses that line.

two_identity_paths: A tokenized <Phrase> key is a MARKER STRING, so it encodes nesting and is sensitive to any tree difference. A content block's custom_id is a flat ORDERED TOKEN ARRAY, so it survives a tree difference that preserves document order. Measured consequence: foster parenting splits the phrase key ONLY, while a raw-text body carrying markup splits BOTH - and the block half is an ARITY change, which per CID-1 re-keys every block containing one. The raw-text family is therefore the more damaging of the two, which is the opposite of this file's first reading.
provenance: libxml2 columns are MEASURED in this repo, on libxml2 2.9.13 only (see libxml2_version). JS-family PHRASE keys (the encoded strings) are MEASURED: langsys-js-server @ 8105faa, real Chromium 153 against parse5, 9/9, and re-run by the Reviewer against the JS Server's own encodePhrase(). NOT Chromium: for token arrays the Chromium half remains unmeasured, and Chromium evidence here is the phrase keys only. Separately, and still true: the TS lane's test DOM (happy-dom) builds a raw-text body the libxml2 way, so TS's own tests cannot see the raw-text split this file records.
block_id_category: UI. Every *_block_id in this file is HtmlParser::generateCustomId('UI', tokens). The category is PART OF THE HASH, so the ids are not reproducible without it - under the SDK's default '__uncategorized__' the same tokens give different values (e.g. foster-stray-element becomes b67f0bc9259c1341bcca9555db386076). Stated because an id a reader cannot recompute from this file is not evidence.
